ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal operational amplifier negative feedback circuit. The output terminal is connected back to the inverting input terminal through the feedback resistor R_F; the inverting input terminal is also grounded through the resistor R1. The input voltage u_i first passes through the resistor R2 to the non-inverting input terminal, and the non-inverting input terminal is then grounded through the resistor R3, so the non-inverting terminal is driven by the R2-R3 voltage divider. The output voltage u_o is marked on the right side. Reasoning: Under negative feedback, an ideal op-amp can be treated as a non-inverting amplifier circuit. The non-inverting input terminal voltage is v_+ = u_i * R3 / (R2 + R3). Substituting u_i = 5 mV, R2 = 1 kΩ, R3 = 200 Ω gives v_+ = 5 * 200 / (1000 + 200) mV = 5/6 mV. The inverting terminal feedback network is R_F-R1, so the non-inverting amplification factor is 1 + R_F/R1 = 1 + 1000/200 = 6. Therefore u_o = 6 * (5/6) mV = 5 mV.

Substitute u_i=5 mV, R2=1 kΩ, R3=200Ω, R_F=1 kΩ, R1=200Ω to get u_o=6*(5/6)mV=5 mV.
